summary: The note is a collection of excerpts about the Qing dynasty (1644–1912), the last imperial dynasty of China. It covers the Manchu conquest after the fall of the Ming, the Eight Banners military system, sources of legitimacy, frontier policy and Han settlement of Manchuria, and the 19th-century crises (Taiping Rebellion, foreign wars, Boxers, Cixi's regencies). It ends with the 1911 Wuchang Uprising and the 1912 abdication of Puyi.
one_line: Overview of the Qing dynasty from the 1644 Manchu conquest through its institutions, frontier policy and 19th-century crises to Puyi's 1912 abdication.
key_facts: The Qing dynasty, officially the Great Qing, ruled China from 1644 to 1912, with a brief abortive restoration in 1917; it was preceded by the Ming and succeeded by the Republic of China.
Nurhaci declared himself 'Bright Khan' of the Later Jin state, and his son Hong Taiji renamed the dynasty Great Qing in 1636.
In April 1644 Li Zicheng's rebels sacked Beijing and the Chongzhen Emperor committed suicide; Wu Sangui allied with Dorgon and they defeated Li Zicheng on May 27, 1644.
Dorgon made Beijing the dynastic capital and reappointed most Ming officials, which helped stabilize the regime quickly.

The Eight Banners, first developed by Nurhaci, were divided into the 'Upper Three Banners' under the emperor and the 'Lower Five Banners' commanded by hereditary Manchu princes; the Green Standard Army, made of surrendered Ming troops, eventually outnumbered Banner troops three to one.
400,000 Green Standard Army soldiers and 200,000 Bannermen were used against the Three Feudatories.

Zeng Guofan organized the Xiang Army, a hybrid militia and standing army, during the Taiping Rebellion after the loss of Nanjing in 1853; it and the Huai Army of Li Hongzhang were collectively called the 'Yong Ying' (Brave Camp).
In 1756 the Qing established the Canton System, restricting maritime trade to Canton and giving monopoly rights to private Chinese merchants.
The Sino-French War ended in 1885 with the Treaty of Tientsin (1885), in which China recognized the French protectorate in Vietnam.

Xinjiang became a province in 1884 after Yaqub Beg's rule in Kashgaria was defeated; Manchuria was turned into three provinces in the early 20th century, bringing the total number of regional viceroys to nine.
Cixi came to power in 1861 after her five-year-old son became the Tongzhi Emperor; she became sole regent after Ci'an died in the spring of 1881.
The Boxers besieged the Foreign Legation Quarter in 1900, and Cixi declared war on the Eight-Nation Alliance, lost Beijing and fled to Xi'an.
The Guangxu Emperor died on November 14, 1908 and Cixi on November 15; an autopsy nearly a century later confirmed lethal levels of arsenic in his corpse.
On 12 February 1912 Longyu issued an edict bringing about the abdication of the child emperor Puyi, ending over 2,000 years of Imperial China.

entities.name: Qing dynasty
entities.role: last imperial dynasty of China, 1644–1912, also called the Manchu dynasty

entities.name: Nurhaci
entities.role: founder of the Later Jin state and the Eight Banners system

entities.name: Hong Taiji
entities.role: son of Nurhaci who renamed the dynasty Great Qing in 1636 and added Mongol and Han Banners

entities.name: Dorgon
entities.role: Manchu leader who allied with Wu Sangui and made Beijing the capital

entities.name: Wu Sangui
entities.role: Ming general at Shanhai Pass who allied with the Manchus and was given Yunnan and Guizhou

entities.name: Li Zicheng
entities.role: rebel leader who sacked Beijing in 1644 and founded the short-lived Shun dynasty

entities.name: Chongzhen Emperor
entities.role: last Ming ruler, committed suicide when Beijing fell

entities.name: Zeng Guofan
entities.role: Chinese official who organized the Xiang Army against the Taipings

entities.name: Li Hongzhang
entities.role: colleague and mentee of Zeng Guofan who created the Huai Army

entities.name: Cixi
entities.role: Empress Dowager who dominated the court as regent and declared war on the Eight-Nation Alliance

entities.name: Guangxu Emperor
entities.role: Cixi's nephew, emperor who died in 1908, apparently poisoned with arsenic

entities.name: Puyi
entities.role: last Qing emperor, abdicated in 1912 and became emperor of Manchukuo in 1932

entities.name: Yuan Shikai
entities.role: general who commanded the Beiyang Army and became Prime Minister in 1911

entities.name: Sun Yat-sen
entities.role: provisional head of the Republic of China in Nanjing

entities.name: Longyu
entities.role: Empress Dowager who issued the abdication edict in 1912

entities.name: Zaifeng
entities.role: Prince Chun, regent for Puyi and father of Puyi

entities.name: Kangxi Emperor
entities.role: Qing emperor who welcomed Jesuit missionaries to his court

entities.name: Qianlong
entities.role: Qing emperor who projected an image as a Buddhist sage ruler and patron of Tibetan Buddhism

entities.name: Yaqub Beg
entities.role: invader of Xinjiang who ruled the kingdom of Kashgaria with British support

entities.name: Taiping Rebellion
entities.role: mid-19th-century rebellion that caused disastrous Qing defeats

entities.name: Boxers
entities.role: Righteous and Harmonious Fists, who besieged the Foreign Legation Quarter in 1900

entities.name: Eight-Nation Alliance
entities.role: coalition of European, Japanese and Russian armies that entered China in 1900

entities.name: Wuchang Uprising
entities.role: October 10, 1911 uprising that led to creation of the Republic of China

entities.name: Manchukuo
entities.role: state founded by Japan in 1932 in Northeast China with Puyi as emperor

entities.name: Eight Banners
entities.role: Manchu military and social organization created by Nurhaci

entities.name: Canton System
entities.role: 1756 policy restricting maritime trade to Canton
